This authentic Indian dinner recipe brings the magic of the tandoor to your backyard, promising a culinary adventure with every bite. instructions.title: Prepare the Chicken
instructions.text: Wash and pat dry the chicken pieces thoroughly. Make deep slits on each piece to allow the marinade to penetrate well. In a large bowl, combine 1 tbsp ginger garlic paste, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 1/2 tsp red chili powder, and 1/2 tsp salt. Rub this mixture all over the chicken pieces. Let it rest for 15-20 minutes.

instructions.title: Prepare the Marinade
instructions.text: In a separate bowl, whisk together the plain yogurt, remaining ginger garlic paste, remaining lemon juice, red chili powder, turmeric powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, garam masala, salt, kasoori methi, and food color (if using). Ensure the marinade is smooth and well combined.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: Add the chicken pieces to the yogurt marinade, ensuring each piece is fully coated. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, for best flavor and tenderness. The longer the marinade, the better the result.

instructions.title: Prepare the Charcoal Grill
instructions.text: Set up your charcoal grill for direct medium-high heat. Allow the charcoal to heat until it is ash-covered and glowing red. Clean the grill grates thoroughly and lightly oil them to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Grill the Chicken
instructions.text: Place the marinated chicken pieces directly over the hot coals. Grill for 6-8 minutes per side, turning occasionally, until the chicken is cooked through and has beautiful char marks. Baste with a mixture of melted butter and mustard oil during the last 10 minutes of cooking.

instructions.title: Check Doneness and Serve
instructions.text: To ensure doneness, insert a meat thermometer into the thickest part of the chicken; it should read 165F (74C). Remove the chicken from the grill. Garnish with fresh cilantro and lemon wedges. Serve hot with naan bread, rice, or a fresh salad.

tips: For extra smoky flavor, add a small piece of wood chip to your charcoal while grilling.
Do not skip the double marination process; it is key to tender and flavorful Tandoori Chicken.
Always allow the chicken to come to room temperature for about 30 minutes before grilling for more even cooking.
article:
Embark on a culinary journey to the vibrant streets of India right from your backyard with the tantalizing aroma and irresistible flavor of Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled. This iconic Indian dinner recipe, traditionally cooked in a clay tandoor oven, translates beautifully to a charcoal grill, imparting a smoky depth and delicious char that elevates the dish to new heights. Forget bland chicken; we're talking about succulent, spice-infused pieces with a fiery red hue and a taste that will transport your senses. Perfect for a weekend gathering or a special family meal, mastering Tandoori Chicken on the grill is a rewarding experience that promises incredible flavor.

## What is Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled?
Tandoori Chicken is a classic South Asian dish where chicken is marinated in yogurt and a blend of aromatic spices, then traditionally cooked at high heat in a tandoor, a cylindrical clay oven. The yogurt acts as a tenderizer, while the spices – including ginger, garlic, cumin, coriander, and often a touch of red chili powder and food coloring – create its distinctive flavor and vibrant color. When adapted for a charcoal grill, the dish takes on an extra dimension. The direct heat of the charcoal sears the outside, locking in juices, while the smoke infuses the chicken with an incomparable smoky essence that a conventional oven simply cannot replicate. The result is perfectly cooked, juicy chicken with a beautiful char and a robust, spicy flavor profile.

## Ingredients You Need
To create this magnificent Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled dish, gather the following:

For the Chicken:
*   1.5 kg (about 3-3.5 lbs) whole chicken, cut into 8 pieces (or 8 chicken thighs/drumsticks)
*   2-3 deep slits on each chicken piece (to allow marinade to penetrate)

For the Marinade:
*   1 cup (240g) plain full-fat yogurt (Greek yogurt works well for a thicker marinade)
*   2 tablespoons ginger-garlic paste (equal parts fresh ginger and garlic, crushed)
*   1 tablespoon lemon juice
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color, or cayenne for heat)
*   1 teaspoon ground cumin
*   1 teaspoon ground coriander
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1/2 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/4 teaspoon black pepper
*   1/4 teaspoon red food coloring (optional, for authentic color)
*   1 tablespoon dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi), crushed (optional, but highly recommended for authentic flavor)
*   Salt to taste (start with 1 teaspoon)
*   2 tablespoons mustard oil (or any neutral oil like vegetable oil)

For Grilling:
*   Charcoal briquettes or lump charcoal
*   Grilling skewers (metal skewers are best)
*   Oil for basting (melted butter or a mix of oil and lemon juice)

## How to Make Tandoori Chicken Marinade
The marinade is the heart and soul of Tandoori Chicken, imparting both flavor and tenderness.
1.  **Prepare the Chicken**: Wash the chicken pieces thoroughly and pat them completely dry with paper towels. Make 2-3 deep slits on each piece using a sharp knife. This helps the marinade penetrate deeply.
2.  **Combine Wet Ingredients**: In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the plain yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, and lemon juice until smooth. The yogurt's acidity helps tenderize the chicken.
3.  **Add Dry Spices**: Stir in the red chili powder, ground cumin, ground coriander, turmeric powder, garam masala, black pepper, and salt. If using, add the red food coloring and crushed kasoori methi. Mix everything thoroughly until a smooth, vibrant paste forms.
4.  **Incorporate Oil**: Finally, mix in the mustard oil. Mustard oil is traditional and adds a pungent depth of flavor, but a neutral oil can be used if preferred.
5.  **Marinate the Chicken**: Add the prepared chicken pieces to the marinade. Using your hands (gloves recommended, especially with food coloring), massage the marinade into every piece, ensuring it gets into all the slits.
6.  **Refrigerate**: Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight (12-24 hours) for the best flavor and tenderness. The longer the chicken marinates, the more flavorful and succulent your Tandoori Chicken will be.

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Charcoal Grilling
Grilling Tandoori Chicken on charcoal requires a bit of attention but yields incredible results.
1.  **Prepare Your Grill**: Arrange charcoal in your grill for two-zone cooking: a hot side with a concentrated pile of coals and a cooler side with fewer coals or no coals. Light the charcoal and let it heat up until it's covered in a light gray ash, indicating it's ready for cooking. This usually takes 20-30 minutes.
2.  **Skewer the Chicken**: While the grill heats, thread the marinated chicken pieces onto metal skewers. Don't overcrowd them; leave a little space between each piece to ensure even cooking. If you don't have skewers, you can place the chicken directly on the grill grates.
3.  **Clean and Oil Grates**: Once the grill is hot, clean the grates with a wire brush and then lightly oil them to prevent sticking.
4.  **Sear the Chicken**: Place the skewered chicken directly over the hot side of the grill. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side, turning frequently, until you get a nice char and color. This initial high heat helps to lock in moisture and develop that desirable smoky crust.
5.  **Move to Cooler Zone**: Once seared, move the chicken to the cooler side of the grill. Close the lid (if your grill has one) to allow the chicken to cook through indirectly. This prevents the outside from burning before the inside is cooked.
6.  **Cook Indirectly**: Cook for another 15-25 minutes, turning the skewers every 5-7 minutes. Baste the chicken periodically with a little melted butter or oil-lemon juice mixture to keep it moist and add flavor.
7.  **Check for Doneness**: Tandoori Chicken is cooked when its internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C) using a meat thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the chicken, avoiding the bone. The juices should run clear.
8.  **Final Sear (Optional)**: If you desire more char, you can move the chicken back over the hot coals for a minute or two on each side just before removing it from the grill.
9.  **Rest**: Transfer the cooked chicken to a platter, cover loosely with foil, and let it rest for 5-10 minutes. This allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring a more tender and flavorful result.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results
Achieving perfect Tandoori Chicken is all about technique and a few insider secrets.
*   **Dry the Chicken**: Always pat the chicken thoroughly dry before marinating. Excess moisture prevents the marinade from adhering and the skin from crisping.
*   **Marination Time is Key**: Don't skimp on marination time. At least 4 hours is good, but overnight (12-24 hours) truly makes a difference in flavor penetration and tenderness.
*   **Two-Zone Grilling**: This is crucial for Tandoori Chicken. Searing over high heat for color and char, then finishing over indirect heat prevents burning and ensures even cooking.
*   **Don't Overcrowd**: Give your chicken pieces space on the grill for even cooking and proper airflow.
*   **Use a Thermometer**: A meat thermometer is your best friend. It takes the guesswork out of grilling and ensures your chicken is perfectly cooked and safe to eat without being dry.
*   **Basting**: Basting with melted butter or oil during the indirect cooking phase adds moisture and a rich flavor.

## Serving Suggestions
Tandoori Chicken is a star on its own, but it truly shines when paired with traditional Indian accompaniments. Serve it hot off the grill with:
*   **Naan Bread**: Warm, fluffy naan is perfect for scooping up the flavorful chicken and any leftover juices.
*   **Raita**: A cooling yogurt dip with cucumber and mint provides a refreshing contrast to the spicy chicken.
*   **Lemon Wedges and Sliced Onions**: A squeeze of fresh lemon juice brightens the flavors, and raw onion slices add a pleasant crunch and bite.
*   **Mint Chutney or Green Chutney**: These fresh, spicy, and tangy chutneys are classic pairings.
*   **Basmati Rice**: A simple side of fragrant basmati rice complements the meal beautifully.
*   **Fresh Salad**: A simple kachumber salad (diced cucumber, tomato, onion with lemon and cilantro) adds freshness.

## Variations and Substitutions
While the classic Tandoori Chicken recipe is a winner, feel free to experiment:
*   **Different Proteins**: This marinade works wonderfully with other proteins. Try it with paneer (Indian cheese) for a vegetarian option, fish fillets, shrimp, or even lamb chops. Adjust cooking times accordingly.
*   **Spice Level**: Adjust the amount of red chili powder to suit your preference for heat. For a milder version, reduce or omit chili powder and rely on black pepper for a gentle warmth. For more heat, add a pinch of cayenne.
*   **Smokiness**: If you don't have a charcoal grill, you can use a gas grill or even an oven. For an oven-baked version, cook at 400°F (200°C) until done, then broil for a few minutes for char. To add smokiness, you can use liquid smoke in the marinade or finish with a quick smoking method using a piece of hot charcoal and oil in a separate bowl inside a covered pot.
*   **Herbs**: Experiment with fresh herbs like cilantro or mint, finely chopped and added to the marinade for an extra layer of freshness.

Mastering Tandoori Chicken on your charcoal grill is a culinary accomplishment that will impress family and friends alike. The smoky aroma, the vibrant color, and the explosion of flavors make this an unforgettable Indian dinner recipe. So fire up your grill, embrace the spices, and prepare to enjoy one of India's most beloved dishes right in your own home.
